statement: For a strict fibred category C→T and a cofinal sequence t:N^op→T, put C_t=C×_T N^op; localization of its cartesian arrows gives the sequential colimit C_∞.
repair: The ordinary colimit is computed from the strict sequence of fibre categories.
notes: The sequence is cofinal in the preorder T_o; this is not automatically homotopy cofinal in T.

statement: The roof C←C_t→C_∞ yields an isomorphism in Hot if both legs are weak equivalences.
repair: Formal localization argument.
notes: The source is discussing a sufficient comparison mechanism; it does not rule out unrelated equivalences.

statement: For T=N^op, does the canonical localization C→colim_n C_n induce a weak equivalence?
repair: Yes. The comma-category proof in commentary p108 applies to every strict sequential diagram.
notes: Answered affirmatively in the following source paragraph.

statement: For every sequential system of small categories, the functor from its fibred Grothendieck construction over N^op to its ordinary colimit is a weak equivalence.
gap_or_error: The source announces conviction without giving the proof here.
repair: Complete finite-diagram contraction of every q/z is supplied in commentary p108.
notes: No injectivity or full-faithfulness assumption on transitions is needed.

statement: The preceding weak equivalence defines a morphism C_∞→C in Hot by the roof C_∞←C_t→C.
repair: Invert the horizontal weak equivalence in Hot.
notes: This does not define a functor C_∞→C in Cat.

statement: Is the canonical morphism C_∞→C always an isomorphism in Hot?
repair: No under the general hypotheses; take C=T=BG for a nontrivial group and a sequence constant on the identity. Then C_∞=* and the comparison is *→BG.
notes: The geometric all-arrows case is settled positively in §13, ms157–169.

statement: A cofiltered countably coinitial preorder T_o does not imply that BT is contractible.
repair: The one-object category BG has preorder a point and fundamental group G.
notes: The source supplies the one-object mechanism; the commentary specifies a nontrivial group.

statement: Under the homotopy hypothesis for parallel reindexings, C, C_∞ and the ind-object H_C have the same set of connected components.
repair: Connected components of the total category are the colimit of fibre components over T^op; the homotopy hypothesis factors this set-valued diagram through T_o^op, and a cofinal sequence computes that colimit.
notes: This statement retains no higher homotopy information.

statement: The total path category is provisionally considered dispensable except for its connected components.
repair: This is a working assessment, reversed by the strict path comparison in §13.
notes: Not a mathematical nonexistence theorem.

statement: Concatenation of all finite path types gives a strictly associative bifunctor on composable path categories, with empty paths as units.
repair: Follows from the strict concatenation formalism of §§7–9 and earlier VII-a commentary at ms48–53.
notes: The product is over the common endpoint; for based loops it is an ordinary product.

statement: A fixed colimit presentation C_∞ does not immediately supply a canonical associative composition, whereas the corresponding ind-objects have a composition in Ind Cat hot.
repair: Binary composition is constructed at ms125–127 using opposite padding conventions. For all arrows, §13 returns to strict all-types concatenation.
notes: The statement describes the stage of the construction, not an impossibility theorem.

statement: If T→T_o is smooth and coaspherical, or proper and aspherical, the desired base-change comparison C_t→C is a weak equivalence.
gap_or_error: No proof is reproduced on these pages; it uses the earlier base-change/asphericity results.
repair: Read as the sufficient criterion asserted using the preceding localizer calculus, not as a necessary condition.
notes: Smooth/proper are Grothendieck localizer notions; they are not ordinary categorical fibrations/cofibrations.

statement: The comparison is valid when T=T_o is a cofiltered preorder.
repair: A coinitial sequence is homotopy coinitial in the cofiltered preorder, and the fibred Grothendieck construction computes the appropriate homotopy colimit.
notes: The parallel-arrow obstruction vanishes in a preorder.

statement: The functor Ty→Ty_o is neither smooth nor proper, not even for the connectedness localizer.
gap_or_error: The assertion is stated without proof in the supplied source; the commentary supplies the explicit lifting-category calculation.
repair: Take S=Δ+Δ−Δ+ and T=Δ+. There are exactly two endpoint-preserving type maps S→T and both endomorphism monoids are trivial. Since T_o retains the same objects, both relevant lift categories are discrete two-point categories, hence not connected.
notes: This proves the source assertion without inferring failure of the geometric comparison from failure of a sufficient criterion.

statement: The comparison C_∞→Ch_Σ(X;a,b) is conjectured not to be a weak equivalence in general.
gap_or_error: The argument offered for the all-arrows loop case is false and withdrawn in footnote24.
repair: For Σ=Fl(X), §13 proves the comparison equivalence by the total path category. The argument here establishes no negative conclusion for general Σ.
notes: Do not extend the later all-arrows theorem to arbitrary relative categories without checking admissibility.

statement: The based loop object Ω(BX,a) cannot in general be modeled by a strictly associative simplicial monoid.
gap_or_error: Strict loop-group and Moore-loop models contradict the assertion.
repair: The source corrects itself in footnote24. Kan loop groups give a stronger simplicial-group model; Moore loops give strict associative topological monoids.
notes: The error is in the inference, not in the transcription.

statement: For a reduced simplicial set K, a simplicial group GK models Ω|K| and the unit K→Wbar GK is a weak equivalence.
repair: Kan’s loop-group theorem; verified in the modern proof by Stevenson.
notes: Footnote24 alludes to Quillen; the explicit reducedness hypothesis belongs in the modern statement.

statement: The fibre diagram descends through T_o^op to an ind-object H_T in Cat hot, and similarly after passage to Hot.
repair: Parallel reindexings are equal after taking natural-transformation homotopy classes; cofilteredness of T_o supplies the ind-index.
notes: H_T is not the ordinary colimit category.

statement: The stage maps define H_T→C_∞ in Ind Cat hot and Ind Hot, and a comparison C_∞→C only in Hot in general.
repair: The first map is the colimit cocone; the second is the roof of ms109.
notes: Keep the categories in which the different arrows live separate.

statement: The object of the finite-test presheaf category associated with C_∞ equals the filtered colimit of the stage-representable presheaves.
gap_or_error: Chapter V ms45 defines finite by finite objects and arrows, and ms51–52 defines Hot_0 using those categories. This does not imply homotopy compactness.
repair: Replace Hot_0 by homotopy-finite test types for this colimit formula; retain the separate valid finite-presentation formula in Cat hot.
notes: The source’s convention for finite tests must be stated explicitly.

statement: Concatenation gives functors Ch_{Σ,τ}(a,b)×Ch_{Σ,τ′}(b,c)→Ch_{Σ,ττ′}(a,c).
repair: Concatenate object diagrams and their endpoint-fixed natural transformations.
notes: The stage notation C_n×C_m→C_{n+m} applies to the chosen multiplicative power-type systems.

statement: The naive stage concatenations are compatible with the padding transition maps only up to categorical homotopy.
repair: The new constant blocks occur at different internal positions; the homotopy theorem identifies their reparametrizations in Cat hot.
notes: A homotopy-class compatibility is sufficient for the ind-object, but need not determine a coherent map between ordinary colimits.

statement: The ind-path objects form an associative category object in Ind Cat hot; if Σ=Fl(X), reversal supplies inverse morphisms and makes it a groupoid object.
repair: The finite-string localization calculus and the earlier homotopy theorem yield the unit, associativity and inverse identities.
references: Commentary p117; earlier III–V commentary ms27
notes: Inverses are identities in the localized homotopy category, not strict inverse paths in Cat.

statement: For a test object Y, define H_T^Y(a,b)=Hom_{Ind Cat hot}(Y,H_T(a,b)).
gap_or_error: The printed subscript Cat hot suppresses the ind-category when the target is an ind-object.
repair: Interpret the Hom in Ind Cat hot, using constant embedding for ordinary Y.
notes: For ind-Y the set is defined by the ind-Hom formula, not by an ordinary functor category X(Y).

statement: The sets H_T^Y(a,b), with object set Ob X, form a groupoid if Σ=Fl(X) and a category for a general Σ.
repair: Apply the representable functor Hom(Y,−), which preserves finite products, to the category/groupoid object.
notes: This is formal once the ind-composition laws are established.

statement: For ordinary Y, H_T^Y(a,b) is the Hom set between a_Y and b_Y in Fun(Y,X)[Σ_Y^{-1}], where Σ_Y consists of pointwise Σ natural transformations.
gap_or_error: The display on ms117 omits the superscript Y on H_T.
repair: Restore the superscript in the modern statement; finite localized zigzags impose one uniform stage bound over Y.
references: Commentary p117; earlier III–V commentary ms30–33
notes: The edition slip is retained in the source and recorded separately.

statement: C_∞(t) is said to be isomorphic in Hot for every cofinal sequence t, though initially without canonical isomorphisms.
gap_or_error: The general assertion cannot be inferred from the homotopy hypothesis alone; in particular the stated comparison morphisms need not be equivalences.
repair: The all-arrows path case has a later direct geometric proof. The FI^op example in commentary p121 disproves the general claim that every comparison map is invertible.
notes: The counterexample has abstractly isomorphic colimit objects, but a noninvertible canonical comparison; it directly refutes the morphism assertion.

statement: A natural transformation t→t′ induces a functor C_∞(t′)→C_∞(t); hence t↦C_∞(t) is contravariant.
repair: Take the colimit of the strict natural transformation of fibre diagrams.
notes: The printed arrow Hc→Hot is shorthand for a contrafunctor; the modern domain is Hc^op.

statement: Every natural transformation between cofinal sequences induces a weak equivalence C_∞(t′)→C_∞(t) under the general section10 hypotheses.
gap_or_error: An isomorphism of ind-objects after taking homotopy classes does not imply that the induced map of ordinary colimits is a weak equivalence.
repair: Complete FI^op/symmetric-group counterexample in commentary p121; for the geometric all-arrows construction use the later total path comparison.
notes: The counterexample satisfies strict fibredness, parallel-arrow homotopy, countable coinitiality and a monoidal terminal-unit base.

statement: Any contravariant functor on Hc taking every arrow to an isomorphism factors through Π(Hc)^op.
repair: Universal property of localization at all arrows.
notes: The application to the general C_∞ diagram requires the false blanket premise to be replaced by a valid geometric hypothesis.

statement: If Hc is connected, such an isomorphism-valued functor has isomorphic values; if Π(Hc) is terminal, comparisons induced by zigzags are unique.
repair: Connectivity supplies zigzags; triviality of the fundamental groupoid makes their images independent of the zigzag.
notes: Simple connectivity is sufficient, not logically necessary for a particular functor to have trivial monodromy.

statement: A bifunctor * on T with natural projections t*t′→t,t′ makes the category of cofinal sequences connected.
repair: Pointwise t*t′ is cofinal because it maps to t, and the two projections give a connecting span.
notes: The stronger conclusion is contractibility: fix s and use id←(−*s)→const_s.

statement: If * is a bifunctor with terminal two-sided unit, the two projection maps are obtained by applying the terminal maps in one factor.
repair: Use t*t′→t*1≅t and t*t′→1*t′≅t′ with natural unitors.
notes: Associativity is not needed for the existence of the projections.

statement: Does the induced Hot morphism depend only on the endpoints t,t′ and not on the chosen natural transformation?
repair: For an isomorphism-valued diagram the contraction of Hc proves independence. Under the general homotopy hypothesis alone this fails because some comparisons are not invertible.
notes: The two issues—contractibility of choices and invertibility of the assigned arrows—must not be merged.

statement: On finite-test presheaves every comparison is the canonical identification with the presheaf associated to H_T.
gap_or_error: Chapter V ms45 defines finite by finite objects and arrows, and ms51–52 defines Hot_0 using those categories. This does not imply homotopy compactness.
repair: Replace Hot_0 by homotopy-finite test types for this colimit formula; retain the separate valid finite-presentation formula in Cat hot.
notes: The FI example shows why these identifications do not detect all weak equivalences.

statement: For an isomorphism-valued diagram, the threefold-product diagram gives transitivity of the canonical comparisons.
repair: Apply the diagram and invert its arrows; alternatively use contractibility of the category of sequences.
notes: The source’s diagram argument is valid conditionally. It does not establish its invertibility premise.

statement: Under the geometric weak-equivalence comparisons, C_∞ is a canonical object of Hot with a canonical morphism H_T→C_∞ in Ind Hot.
gap_or_error: Canonicity requires both a valid equivalence theorem and coherence.
repair: The contraction of choices supplies coherence; the all-arrows case receives the geometric equivalence theorem in §13.
notes: No assertion of general canonical equivalence under section10 hypotheses alone.

statement: The map colim_n Hom_Hot(ξ,C_n)→Hom_Hot(ξ,C_∞) is bijective for every ξ∈Hot.
gap_or_error: The PDF actually prints Hot without the needed finite-test restriction; arbitrary source objects are not compact.
repair: Restrict ξ to homotopy-compact finite tests. The increasing finite discrete sets already refute the unrestricted statement.
notes: Edition slip confirmed visually on PDF leaf7.

statement: The comparison maps C_∞(t′)→C_∞(t) are induced by actual functors, not merely roofs in Hot.
repair: They are colimits of strict reindexing functors.
notes: This does not make them weak equivalences.

statement: In the geometric case the comparison maps associated with t*t′→t,t′ are fully faithful.
repair: Padding a path by constant segments is fully faithful: a ladder on the padded paths is uniquely determined by its original part and the fixed endpoint components.
notes: This stronger geometric feature is absent from the FI^op counterexample.

statement: A comparison is an ind-isomorphism in Cat hot and consequently induces bijections on finite Cat hot tests.
repair: An ind-isomorphism gives equal values on all constant test objects; finite presentation identifies these values with the colimit-category test sets.
notes: The word homomorphism in the printed proof must be strengthened to isomorphism, as ms122(c) explicitly does.

statement: Bijectivity on all unpointed finite homotopy test sets implies that a map is an isomorphism in Hot.
gap_or_error: Free homotopy classes discard basepoint/conjugacy information; no set of unpointed test spaces is conservative.
repair: Use based tests at all basepoints, the homotopy 2-category, or a direct geometric proof.
notes: Earlier III–V commentary ms52 already gives the finite symmetric-group shift example.

statement: Hom_Hot(Y,−) commutes with filtered colimits whenever Y is a finite category.
gap_or_error: False for the modern convention finite objects and arrows: B(Z/2) has infinite-dimensional nerve and is not compact.
repair: Require BY to have finite CW homotopy type, or explicitly require compactness. Counterexample using RP^n⊂RP^∞ in commentary p121.
notes: This is the source’s explicit convention in Chapter V ms45, not merely a possible modern interpretation.

statement: A filtered colimit of Thomason-fibrant categories is Thomason-fibrant.
repair: Ex^2N preserves filtered colimits; Kan horn fillers use finite domains and codomains.
notes: This does not prove compactness for every finite category; a cofibrant or homotopy-finite source is still needed.

statement: For finite Y, the comparison induces a bijection [Y,C_∞(t′)]_cat→[Y,C_∞(t)]_cat, both being H_T(Y).
repair: Finite functors and finite zigzags of natural transformations descend to a common stage.
notes: This valid Cat hot calculation is distinct from finite-Hot-test conservativity.

statement: Are all comparison functors invertible already in Cat hot?
repair: No in the general fibred setting: the FI^op comparison is not even invertible in Hot, hence cannot be invertible in Cat hot. The stronger question for the specific geometric padding functors is not answered by this counterexample.
notes: No claim is made that the geometric stronger question is an open research problem today; a definitive literature theorem was not located.

statement: For a cofinal sequence t, define C_n(t)=C_{t_n} and C_∞(t)=colim_n C_n(t).
repair: Strict cleavage makes this an ordinary sequential diagram.
notes: Summary item(a), audited again for completeness.

statement: Both the sequential diagram and its colimit depend contravariantly on the sequence, and product sequences compare any two choices.
repair: Pointwise reindexing and natural projections.
notes: Summary item(b); same content as ms117–119.

statement: The ind-object (C_n(t)) is canonically independent of t, and comparison morphisms are compatible with its common identification H.
repair: The homotopy hypothesis factors the diagram through the cofiltered preorder; cofinal changes compute the same ind-object.
notes: Unique here means unique under the specified common ind-presentation, not absence of all automorphisms.

statement: The ind-identification implies that all induced comparison maps on C_∞ are isomorphisms in Hot.
gap_or_error: Repeats the invalid inference of ms117–121.
repair: The FI^op example gives a non-surjective shift on fundamental groups despite an ind-isomorphism.
notes: Summary item(d) is false at the generality stated.

statement: After valid weak-equivalence comparisons, a monoidal product of sequences gives a transitive system of canonical isomorphisms.
repair: Use the source’s threefold diagram or the stronger contraction lemma.
notes: The assertion is conditional; the monoidal structure alone does not guarantee weak equivalences.

statement: The ind-object H is generally not essentially constant, so H→C_∞ need not be an isomorphism in Ind Hot.
repair: Increasing finite discrete sets give a complete example; eventual constancy gives positive special cases.
notes: The phrase practically never is qualitative, not a universal quantified assertion.

statement: The restriction H_0 of H to the source’s finite-category test subcategory is represented by the presheaf h(C_∞).
gap_or_error: Chapter V ms45 defines finite by finite objects and arrows, and ms51–52 defines Hot_0 using those categories. This does not imply homotopy compactness.
repair: Replace Hot_0 by homotopy-finite test types for this colimit formula; retain the separate valid finite-presentation formula in Cat hot.
notes: This is restricted representability, not an ind-isomorphism.

statement: If restricted Yoneda Hot→widehat(Hot_0) were fully faithful, H_0 would determine C_∞ up to the unique compatible isomorphism.
repair: Formal full-faithfulness/Yoneda argument.
notes: The antecedent is false for finite tests; the conditional statement itself is valid.

statement: The existence of inverse functors in Cat for the geometric comparisons is not established.
repair: Weak equivalences do not automatically supply actual inverse functors or inverses in Cat hot.
notes: This is an accurately delimited limitation of the source proof.

statement: Does a binary path composition C_∞(a,b)×C_∞(b,c)→C_∞(a,c) exist canonically in Hot?
repair: The source constructs one in ms125–127 using different padding conventions, subject to valid canonical comparisons.
notes: The ind-composition and its finite-test image exist earlier.

statement: The finite-test images have associative composition, units and, for Σ=Fl(X), inverses.
repair: Apply restriction to the ind-category/groupoid structure.
notes: This cannot alone lift the equalities to Hot.

statement: Choose τ_0 of useful length at least2; use t_n=t′_n=τ_0^n with transitions π_p*id and id*π_p, respectively.
repair: The two choices pad at opposite external ends.
notes: The degeneracy π_p:τ_0^p→1 is the total collapse.

statement: The product sequence t″=t*t′ has t″_n=τ_0^{2n} and transition π_p*id_{τ_0^{2n}}*π_p.
repair: Concatenate the two transition formulas and use strict associativity of the interval-type monoid.
notes: This sequence pads both outer ends.

statement: The stage concatenations C_n(t;a,b)×C_n(t′;b,c)→C_n(t″;a,c) commute strictly with transitions.
repair: The equation (1_a^p*c)*(d*1_c^p)=1_a^p*(c*d)*1_c^p also holds for ladders.
notes: This is the successful binary construction.

statement: Strict stage compatibility induces a functor C_∞(t;a,b)×C_∞(t′;b,c)→C_∞(t″;a,c).
repair: Filtered colimits in Cat commute with finite products; the diagonal N→N×N is cofinal.
notes: No appeal to restricted Yoneda is needed at this step.

statement: A morphism τ_0→τ′_0 induces a commutative comparison square of the binary-composition functors.
repair: Functoriality of reindexing and concatenation gives the square in Cat.
notes: The induced vertical arrows are identities only after valid coherent identifications in Hot.

statement: Two unrelated interval types can be compared by their categorical product τ_0×τ′_0 as another interval type.
gap_or_error: The printed cartesian-product symbol is not generally an interval: two nontrivial intervals have a grid product.
repair: Use their concatenation τ_0*τ′_0 with the two collapse maps.
notes: Treated as a source/edition notation slip and retained in the transcription.

statement: After canonical weak-equivalence identifications, the binary composition is independent of τ_0.
repair: Use the strict square for a type morphism and a common concatenation refinement.
notes: The proof presupposes the geometric comparison theorem.

statement: Is the constructed binary operation associative in Hot?
repair: For all arrows, compare with the strictly associative all-types concatenation through the §13 equivalences, including compatibility of the comparison maps.
references: GrothendieckDerivateursVII, ms157–169; commentary p126; development p169, Why the comparison preserves composition
notes: The source leaves the binary construction’s associativity unfinished here; restricted finite tests cannot settle it.

statement: Is Hot→widehat(Hot_0) faithful, or even fully faithful?
repair: No for finite homotopy tests, and no for tests by finite categories: the explicit telescope phantom map in commentary p127 is nonzero but induces the zero natural transformation.
references: Hatcher2002, Examples3F.7 and3F.9 and Theorem4.57; commentary p127
notes: The example is worked out completely in the commentary.

statement: The binary composition is compatible with that on H(a,b) through the maps H(a,b)→C_∞(a,b).
repair: Follows at the stage level from the same concatenation formulas and their colimit cocones.
notes: A compatibility statement does not make the cocone an epimorphism.

statement: If the maps H→C_∞ were epimorphisms stable under products, associativity of the ind-composition would imply associativity in Hot.
repair: Cancel the product of the three epimorphisms from the equality of the two composites.
notes: The proposed sufficient condition is formal and valid.

statement: Are the canonical maps H→C_∞ epimorphisms in Ind Hot, and do they remain so after products?
repair: They need not be epimorphisms: H=(T_n) for the degree-two circle telescope and its essential phantom f:T→K(Z,2) give fH=0H but f≠0.
notes: Failure of the first condition suffices; no separate product counterexample is needed.

statement: Compatibility with a known associative simplicial or topological path model would establish associativity of the categorical construction.
repair: A comparison must respect the binary operation and all choices needed to identify its iterates.
references: Stevenson2012, Theorem21; commentary p128; development p169, Why the comparison preserves composition
notes: An equivalence of underlying spaces without multiplicative compatibility is insufficient.

statement: Kan replacement is proposed as a way to compose direct simplicial paths by passing through a two-step interval and restricting to its long edge.
gap_or_error: The proposal does not specify the filler or its coherence: two edges alone give only the spine of Δ².
repair: Use Kan horn fillers with higher coherence, or a strict simplicial-group/Moore-path model. The categorical interval [2] and the simplicial spine must be distinguished.
notes: The source is exploring a possible construction, not stating a finished theorem; do not count this as a proved false theorem.

statement: For a non-Kan simplicial set K, the strict endpoint fibres of K^{Δ^1}→K×K need not be the derived path spaces.
repair: True: for K=N(0→1←2), the strict fibre over (0,2) is empty but the derived path space is contractible.
notes: Do not strengthen this to a failure of the total-space equivalence K^{Δ^1}≃K, which follows from interval contraction.

statement: A correct simple path construction for finite simplicial sets would imply a finite computation of all their homotopy groups.
gap_or_error: No algorithm or complexity argument is supplied, and existence of a finite model does not imply a terminating computation of all homotopy groups.
repair: Replace this motivation by the explicit strict-fibre counterexample; it proves exactly the needed failure.
notes: The source presents this as a recollection, not a proved undecidability assertion.

statement: For Σ=Fl(X), a weak equivalence X→Xbar should induce Ch_∞(X;a,b)≃Ch_∞(Xbar;a,b).
repair: The all-arrows path-fibre theorem identifies both with the derived path space of BX and B Xbar; weak equivalences preserve these homotopy fibres.
notes: The source discusses a Thomason-fibrant replacement, but the derived-path formulation applies to any weak equivalence with transported endpoints.

statement: For a relative category (M,Sigma), D(Y)=Fun(Y,M)[Sigma_Y^{-1}], with objectwise weak equivalences, defines a prederivator.
gap_or_error: The notation X(Y) is the strict functor category, not its derived replacement.
repair: Retain this distinction throughout the section.
notes: The source recalls rather than reproves the construction.

statement: The external-Hom parameter functor F_{a,b}(Y)=Hom_{D(Y)}(a_Y,b_Y) should send nerve weak equivalences of Y to bijections.
gap_or_error: Necessary for representation by a space; not alone a complete derivator axiom.
repair: For locally constant diagrams in model categories this holds by Cisinski Theorem1.3.
notes: The source proposes a necessary requirement, not a sufficient characterization.

statement: H(a,b)=(Ch_{n,Sigma}(a,b))_n is the ind-object whose evaluation on Y is colim_n pi_0 Fun(Y,Ch_{n,Sigma}(a,b)).
repair: Keep Cat hot distinct from its weak-equivalence localization Hot.
notes: Earlier construction recalled.

statement: Ch_{infty,Sigma}(a,b)=colim_n Ch_{n,Sigma}(a,b) in Cat.
repair: A filtered categorical colimit; evaluation on an infinite parameter need not have a common stage.

statement: The source infers under its locality hypothesis that the finite-parameter evaluation of H(a,b) is [Y,Ch_{infty,Sigma}(a,b)] in Hot, using finite-category compactness.
gap_or_error: The finite-category compactness premise is false: finite means finite Ob and Fl (ChapterV ms.45), which does not imply a finite nerve. This refutes that inference; it does not independently disprove the full conditional conclusion under locality of H. The source also omits Ind and writes a_X,b_X.
repair: Use the localized-diagram presentation theorem, or restrict a filtered-colimit argument to homotopy-finite parameter spaces with the required comparison hypotheses.
notes: Do not infer an unrestricted compactness theorem from finitely many objects and arrows.

statement: A nerve weak equivalence f:X→Xprime should induce weak equivalences Ch_infty(X;a,b)→Ch_infty(Xprime;fa,fb), with all arrows allowed.
gap_or_error: At this point the categorical paths have not yet been identified as homotopy fibres.
repair: Follows once the endpoint fibres are known to model path spaces; the claim belongs to the later comparison theorem.

statement: The path maps induced by a functor f are compatible with the proposed concatenation in Hot.
repair: At finite stages functoriality and concatenation commute strictly; the chosen comparison maps must respect this.

statement: If path spaces are weak-equivalence invariant and the composition is natural, associativity can be tested after a Thomason-fibrant replacement of X.
repair: This conditional reduction is valid; it does not remove the need for a valid path model of the fibrant replacement.

statement: For Thomason-fibrant X, fixed-endpoint paths of type Delta_+ might suffice to model Ch_infty(X;a,b).
gap_or_error: The source retracts the suggestion immediately: that category is discrete and cannot encode higher path homotopy.
repair: Use derived path fibres or the full alternating construction.
notes: Source self-correction: Mais non, ces catégories sont discrètes!

statement: The category of one-arrow paths a→b with identity endpoint transformations is the discrete category Hom_X(a,b).
repair: A square with identities on the two endpoints forces the two arrows to coincide.

statement: Is Hot→Hot_0^wedge faithful, so that finite tests would prove associativity?
repair: The finite-test issues are audited with ms.127 and earlier DER_III-V ms.52; ordinary unbased finite tests do not provide the proposed general criterion.
notes: Source question, not a statement that the matter remains open today.

statement: An external Hom for a,b is an object K whose maps from Y represent Hom_{D(Y)}(a_Y,b_Y), naturally in Y.
gap_or_error: The displayed subscripts a_X,b_X mean a_Y,b_Y.
repair: For a suitable coherent-diagram presentation use K=Map_C(a,b).

statement: If p_! is left adjoint to p^*, then Hom_{D(Y)}(p^*a,p^*b)=Hom_{D(e)}(p_!p^*a,b).
gap_or_error: The source writes M for D(e), although the original M must first be localized.
repair: Read D(e)=M[Sigma^{-1}].
notes: Formal adjunction calculation.

statement: If p_* is right adjoint to p^*, then Hom_{D(Y)}(p^*a,p^*b)=Hom_{D(e)}(a,p_*p^*b).
gap_or_error: Same ambient-category conflation as the preceding formula.
repair: Read the Hom in D(e).

statement: For unrestricted parameter categories the raw uniform-length zigzag functor is retained by H(a,b), rather than automatically by its categorical colimit.
gap_or_error: This construction-level observation does not imply that derived external Hom universally has to be an ind-space.
repair: In a model-category/coherent-diagram presentation one ordinary derived mapping space works for every small parameter.
notes: The ind-object keeps a common zigzag length, which is the relevant issue here.

statement: The proposed external Hom may be defined as the ind-object (Ch_{n,Sigma}(a,b))_n.
repair: This is the source proposal, conditional on its required invariance.

statement: The weak-equivalence invariance of H(a,b) is a genuine restriction, even when Sigma consists of all arrows.

gap_or_error: A quotient in Cat need not have the homotopy type of the corresponding simplicial quotient. No nerve/quotient comparison is supplied.

gap_or_error: Fails already for i=1 in the finite suspension example.

gap_or_error: The proposed family and its n_0=0 starting value do not establish this.

statement: Endpoint-preserving contractions of larger alternating intervals can induce degree-one maps of their circle quotients.
repair: For genuine circle quotients with at least four edges this follows from the explicit traversal; the zero-length quotient is not a circle.

statement: Evaluation Fun(Y,C)×Y→C induces a canonical comparison BFun(Y,C)→RMap(BY,BC).
repair: Nerve preserves finite products; realization and the exponential adjunction give the comparison in the homotopy category.

statement: This absolute comparison is not generally a weak equivalence.
repair: Take Y=B Z and a poset P with BP≃S^1. Fun(B Z,P)≅P is connected, while Map(S^1,S^1) has components indexed by degree.
notes: Worked example in the p135 block.

notes: Complete proof in the p135 block; also compare ms.128.

statement: For any category Y and Thomason-fibrant C, BFun(Y,C) represents RMap(BY,BC).
gap_or_error: Fibrancy of the target does not derive an arbitrary source.
repair: Take Y=B(C2) and a Thomason-fibrant poset P with BP≃B(C2). Fun(Y,P)≅P is connected; the derived mapping space contains distinct constant and equivalence components.
notes: Complete proof in the p136 development.

statement: If C is Thomason-fibrant then Fun(Y,C) is Thomason-fibrant for arbitrary Y.
gap_or_error: Ordinary horn fillers need not respect actions on a diagram.
repair: Construct a countable C2-poset Q whose underlying poset is fibrant and whose fixed points equal the nonfibrant four-object crown D, using free horn cells. The transport category E=Q semidirect C2 is fibrant by trivializing labels over every contractible horn. But Fun(BC2,E)=E coproduct (D×BC2), with D a retract, so it is not fibrant.
notes: Complete original development supplied at p136; independently checked. This proof does not infer failure from non-cartesianness.

statement: Footnote29 requires Thomason cofibrations to remain cofibrations after product with arbitrary Y.
gap_or_error: Taken literally for all cofibrations, this would make every category cofibrant by multiplying empty→point with Y.
repair: Thomason Proposition5.7 shows that cofibrant categories are posets. The additional p136 counterexample also disproves preservation of all trivial cofibrations under product with arbitrary Y, by the lifting adjunction.
notes: The product requirement is a warning in the source, not an established lemma.

statement: For fibrant C and arbitrary Z,Y, pi_0 Fun(Z×Y,C) computes [B(Z×Y),BC].
gap_or_error: Ordinary functors from a noncofibrant source do not exhaust derived morphisms.
repair: The p136 counterexample with Z=e refutes this precise step.

statement: The cartesian closed homotopy category of spaces gives [BZ,RMap(BY,BC)]=[BZ×BY,BC].
repair: This formal adjunction is valid; the two subsequent replacements by pi_0 of strict functor categories are the problem.

statement: Categorical path objects should have the correct homotopy type without first making X Thomason-fibrant.
repair: This is the aim of the endpoint-fibre theorem developed in the remaining pages.

statement: Path categories are intended both to construct external Hom objects and to provide functorial mapping-path replacements in Cat.

statement: The author knows no prederivator not presented by a relative category (M,Sigma).
repair: This records the author’s experience, not a universal presentation theorem for arbitrary prederivators.

statement: For the mapping-path application Sigma_X=Fl(X).
repair: This is a convention for the remainder of the path-space construction.

statement: A fixed projective system t:N^op→Ty defines Ch_infty^t(X) functorially in X.

statement: For the source notion of cofinal sequence of types, cofinality is equivalent to arbitrarily large useful length.

repair: Elementary consequence of the order on reduced interval types.

statement: The source, target and constant-path maps satisfy sigma i=beta i=id_X and p i=diagonal_X.
repair: These identities hold strictly at every chosen stage and at the colimit.

statement: C(f)=Xprime×_{X,sigma}Ch_infty(X), with alpha induced by constant paths and bar f=beta pr_E.
repair: The diagram is an ordinary pullback of categories.

repair: Directly from the pullback and beta i=id.

statement: For every f, bar f in this factorization should be both fibrant and a weak equivalence.
gap_or_error: The unconditional weak-equivalence assertion is attached to the wrong arrow, as item3 explicitly acknowledges.
repair: It is alpha that is a weak equivalence; bar f is one if and only if f is.
notes: Edition slip kept and explained.

statement: The map alpha should be a Thomason cofibration.
gap_or_error: For f=id_[1], a nonconstant path has an incoming map to the constant path1, so the constants inclusion is not a sieve.

statement: Item1: p:Ch_infty(X)→X×X should be smooth, proper and a HOT-fibration.

statement: Assuming the replacement properties, bar f is trivial if and only if f is a weak equivalence.

statement: The reversed system t^o is obtained by reversing interval order and exchanging its endpoints.

notes: This differs from categorical opposite t^-.

statement: Fix t_n=(Delta_+Delta_-)^{2n}, with t_{n+p}→t_n obtained by collapsing p two-edge blocks at each end.

statement: The interval type tau_{n,m} depends only on m-n and the parity of n.
repair: It is the alternating word of that length beginning with sign (-1)^n.

repair: Reversal preserves the word +- and its symmetric collapse maps, whereas sign reversal changes their initial sign.

repair: A one-step translation of finite support intervals gives mutually inverse cofinal reindexings of the two two-sided alternating systems.

statement: There are endpoint-preserving isomorphisms Ch_t(X)≅Ch_{t^-}(X), natural in X.
repair: Translate every bi-infinite path by one place; use the inverse translation for the inverse functor.

statement: The functors satisfy S^2=id and STS^{-1}=T^{-1}.
repair: Substitution verifies these identities on vertices, arrows and natural transformations.

Translation is induced by an automorphism of the pro-object of interval types, though not by a level-preserving automorphism of the displayed projective system.
repair: An asymmetric padding functor on the sequential Grothendieck category realizes even translation; see the development block at p169.

statement: $T^2$ induces the identity on the associated ind-object in $\mathrm{Cat\,hot}$ and hence on its images in $\mathrm{Ind\,Hot}$ and in the finite-test presheaf category.

statement: The endpoint functor $p:\Ch_\infty(X)\to X\times X$ is smooth, proper, and a homotopy fibration.

statement: $\Ch_\infty(X)=\varinjlim_{n\to-\infty,\,m\to+\infty}\Ch_{n,m}(X)$; positive-length even-even and odd-odd endpoint subsequences are cofinal.

statement: For even $n,m$ with $n<m$, the endpoint functor of $\Ch_{n,m}(X)$ is a Grothendieck fibration and hence smooth.
gap_or_error: The printed statement omits the degenerate n=m exception.

statement: Smoothness passes from a filtered diagram of categories over a fixed base to its filtered colimit, even if the transition functors are not Cartesian.

statement: The eventual-path endpoint functor need not be a strict Grothendieck fibration or opfibration.

statement: Properness of the eventual-path endpoint functor follows by categorical duality, equivalently by a cofinal system of intervals whose endpoints are sinks.
repair: Use the odd-odd positive-length supports and the dual filtered-lift argument. This avoids any ambiguous total-Grothendieck duality.

statement: A functor which is both smooth and proper has strict fibres which compute homotopy fibres, and this property survives base change.

statement: The required homotopy-fibration condition can be expressed by requiring $E/b\to E/b^{\prime}$ to be a weak equivalence for every arrow $b\to b^{\prime}$ of the base.

statement: The two vertical fibre inclusions determine a unique morphism $\varphi$ in Hot making the displayed square commute.

statement: Whiskering by the reverse of $u:a\to a^{\prime}$ and by $v:b\to b^{\prime}$ gives an isomorphism between the corresponding path-space homotopy types.

statement: The finite-stage composition operations should make the comparison square commute on associated ind-objects.
gap_or_error: The compatibility calculation is deferred.

statement: The source and target maps $\sigma,\beta:\Ch_\infty(X)\to X$ are trivial homotopy fibrations, equivalently they have weakly contractible strict fibres.

statement: $\Ch_\infty(X;a,?)$ is the filtered colimit of the finite-interval functor categories with value a at the initial vertex.

repair: The truncations r_k(j)=min(j,k) give a finite natural-transformation zigzag fixing the initial vertex. Precomposition contracts the functor category; full proof at p152.

statement: $C(f)=X^{\prime}\times_{X,\sigma}\Ch_\infty(X)$ has objects pairs $(x^{\prime},c)$ satisfying $\sigma(c)=f(x^{\prime})$ and map $\bar f(x^{\prime},c)=\beta(c)$.
notes: Morphisms are pairs compatible with their source-endpoint components, as required by the ordinary pullback.
